speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I’m Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long these skin lesions have been present and if they are itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the lesions flat-topped and do they have a central dimple or umbilication? I would like to examine the distribution of the papules to see if they are localized or widespread.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of pearly papules with central umbilication is classic for molluscum contagiosum. Let me perform a physical examination to confirm the characteristic appearance and distribution of these lesions.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previously healthy, up-to-date immunizations, no significant illnesses. Social history: Attends daycare three times per week.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic presentation of umbilicated papules and daycare exposure, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
